title: Boza service at Vefa Bozacısı
alt: A worker pours boza behind the counter inside Istanbul's Vefa Bozacısı shop
rationale: Actual Vefa shop service makes the drink and its ordinary hospitality setting legible. Selected over a historic exterior and a less focused room view.
depiction: Historical documentary view of service, not today's staff, serving format or an EA visit.

Categories.value: Vefa Bozacısı|Turkey photographs taken on 2015-12-08|Self-published work|December 2015 in Istanbul|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Men at work in Istanbul

ImageDescription.value:
From the Wikipedia article: In 1876, brothers Haci Ibrahim and Haci Sadik established a boza shop in the Istanbul district of Vefa, close to the then center of entertainment, Direklerarası. This boza, with its thick consistency and tart flavor, became famous throughout the city, and is the only boza shop dating from that period still in business today. The firm is now run by Haci Sadik and Haci Ibrahim's great-great-grandchildren. 
The vessel it's poured from is an intermediate one: it's "brewn" in much larger vessels behind the door that's open.

ImageDescription.value: Of all the vantage points at the premises of Wave Hill Public Garden in the Bronx from which to view the Palisades and the Hudson River, the overlook at the west end of the Lower Lawn is the best - but the pergola on the Great Lawn, styled with a profusion of intricately arranged seasonal potted plants into an ambience redolent of a tropical oasis - is the most verdant. ImageDescription.value: Upper chapel of the Sainte-Chapelle, located in the medieval Palais de la Cité (residence of the Kings of France until the 14th century), Île de la Cité in the Seine, Paris, France. It was commissioned by King Louis IX and its construction began sometime after 1238 and the chapel was consecrated on 26 April 1248. The Sainte-Chapelle is considered among the highest achievements of the Rayonnant period of Gothic architecture, and it has one of the most extensive 13th-century stained glass collections anywhere in the world
